subject: Persistent 502/503 spikes in EU & US — impacting FastPay checkout
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fastpay.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>; grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@fastpay.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Persistent 502/503 spikes in EU & US — impacting checkout

Hi Olga / Grace,

We started seeing a severe increase in 502/503 responses and timeouts from Redwood this morning across our EU and US checkout endpoints (~08:50 UTC onward). Customers are experiencing failed payment attempts and the retry logic on our side is causing a huge spike in downstream requests. Sample errors attached (fastpay_502_sample.log).

Key impact:
- Peak 5xx rate ~25% of requests to /v1/generate between 08:50-09:20 UTC.
- Timeouts at load balancer level, followed by 502/503 returned to callers.
- Several merchants reported duplicate charges due to partial retries.

We have an upcoming release scheduled for 12:00 UTC and this is blocking us. Please treat as P1 — need immediate mitigation (rate limiting, fallback routing, or temporary circuit-breaker) and an incident bridge.

Can you confirm receipt and provide ETA for a mitigation plan?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fastpay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:18:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent 502/503 spikes in EU & US — impacting checkout

Acknowledged — we see the same in our telemetry. Marcus and SRE are on it; Grace will coordinate the bridge. Immediate actions we are taking now:

- Rate-limit aggressive client IPs and apply per-route circuit-breaker to reduce retry amplification.
- Shift a subset of traffic from affected EU edge POPs to nearby healthy regions as a temporary failover.
- Increase proxy connect/read timeouts by 200ms to avoid premature 502s.

I will put up a short incident note and send a join link for a 30-min bridge (proposed 13:00 UTC). Marcus — can you confirm root cause hypothesis and whether a configuration change is safe to roll now?

—Olga
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>; grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:35:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent 502/503 spikes in EU & US — impacting checkout

Quick SRE findings so far (initial):

- Correlation with a scheduled cache invalidation job that started at 08:45 UTC. The job caused a fanout of cache misses to origin which increased upstream latency and caused LB healthchecks to flake.
- Proxy error stream shows connection resets between edge and upstream (502) and timeouts on the upstream socket (504).
- A subset of edge POPs reported CPU saturation on the proxy process during the spike window.

Proposed immediate mitigations (safe to roll now):
1) Disable the aggressive cache invalidation job for 1 hour (we have a rollback plan).
2) Apply a temporary 2s upstream timeout and enable per-route queueing to smooth bursts.
3) Add a short-term token-bucket rate limit for high-traffic customers (FastPay included) to keep overall 5xx under control while we stabilize.

I've attached a short log extract and a trace span screenshot (edge-trace-span-20270719.png) showing the long tail on the upstream call. If OK, I'll push the config changes to canary and then to affected POPs.

Attachments: fastpay_502_sample.log (log), edge-trace-span-20270719.png (image)

- Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fastpay.com>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>; marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent 502/503 spikes in EU & US — impacting checkout

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the flag and the sample logs. We are scheduling a 30-minute bridge at 13:00 UTC to walk through our mitigation and timeline (join: https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/fastpay-20270719).

What we'll cover: short incident summary, immediate mitigations (disable cache invalidation, apply back-pressure), expected user impact reduction, and next steps (postmortem/RCA ETA).

I will also open a HubSpot incident note and link it to your account: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/fastpay

Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>; rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>; hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>; marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:05:47 -0700
Subject: Executive summary & approval request — FastPay regional ingress 5xx spike (EU/US)

Team,

Summary (TL;DR): FastPay is experiencing elevated 5xx/429 rates in EU and US due to a cache invalidation job that created a fanout of origin requests, which increased upstream latency and caused edge LB health flapping and retry amplification. Impact is customer-facing (checkouts) and we have merchants reporting duplicate charges.

Actions taken:
- SRE has disabled the cache invalidation job and will roll a temporary upstream timeout & per-route queueing (in canary now).
- Traffic failover from affected EU POPs to healthy neighbors is in progress.
- CS scheduled a customer bridge at 13:00 UTC; we have logs and traces attached.

Request for exec decisions:
1) Authorize a one-time customer credit for outage window (proposed 10% of July committed usage) — need approval to offer now so Grace can close the customer loop.
2) Authorize priority routing capacity to handle FastPay's high QPS during remediation (temporary reserved capacity for 24 hours).

If we don't have approval in 2 hours, Grace will offer a non-committal goodwill credit and we'll follow up with formal approval later.

I will publish a short incident page and follow up with RCA.

—Olga
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fastpay.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>; olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; secops@fastpay.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent 502/503 spikes in EU & US — impacting checkout

Thanks team — appreciate the rapid response. The bridge was helpful and we saw error rates drop after the cache job was disabled. Our ops team will validate charge duplication reports and follow up if we see anything actionable.

We accept the proposed temporary routing and would like confirmation once the reserved capacity is active. Also please send the formal incident timeline and RCA when available — matching logs would help our internal postmortem.

Elena (FastPay SecOps) will coordinate any evidence requests: secops@fastpay.com

—Sanjay
